seeds.title: New issuers' share of new cards, 2023 to 2025
seeds.text: New issuers won 6 to 8% of new credit cards issued in India between 2023 and 2025. Method: issuer-level counts from monthly bank returns. Sample data (simulated).

seeds.title: Firm benchmark: cost to sign up existing customers
seeds.text: Across 12 retail banks, existing customers were signed up for a card 30 to 35% more cheaply than new customers. Method: cost-to-acquire benchmarking study, 2025. Sample data (simulated).

seeds.title: Card numbers to grow 13.8% a year, says forecast (Daily Ledger)
seeds.text: Credit cards in use in India will grow 13.8% a year to 2030, according to the CardScope India Cards Outlook 2026. The forecast was published by CardScope Research this month. Sample data (simulated).

seeds.text: Credit cards in use in India will grow 13.8% a year to 2030, according to the CardScope India Cards Outlook 2026. The forecast was published by CardScope Research this month. Sample data (simulated).

seeds.title: Payment system indicators: credit cards outstanding
seeds.text: Credit cards outstanding stood at 5.53 crore in December 2019 and at 10.80 crore in December 2024. Figures are end-of-month counts reported by banks. Sample data (simulated).

seeds.title: Payment system indicators: credit cards outstanding
seeds.text: Credit cards outstanding stood at 5.53 crore in December 2019 and at 10.80 crore in December 2024. Figures are end-of-month counts reported by banks. (Retrieved a second time.) Sample data (simulated).

seeds.title: Forecast sees card base growing 13.8% a year
seeds.text: Analysts at CardScope expect credit cards in use to grow 13.8% a year, the CardScope India Cards Outlook 2026 shows. Banks are adding cards fastest in large cities. Sample data (simulated).

seeds.title: Why India's card market is booming
seeds.text: India's credit card market is booming and the number of cards is growing 35% a year. Everyone in the industry knows the boom will continue. Sample data (simulated).

seeds.title: New card issuers face long waits for approvals
seeds.text: New card issuers say that setting up a bank arrangement and getting approvals takes about 12 months. Several launches slipped last year. Sample data (simulated).

seeds.title: Forum thread: card growth
seeds.text: Someone on the forum says card numbers will double every year. No source given. Sample data (simulated).

seeds.title: Firm study: card base growth scenarios (2025)
seeds.text: Our 2025 study of 40 issuers estimates that credit cards in use will grow 12 to 18% a year over the next five years. Method: issuer survey and bottom-up model built by the firm. Sample data (simulated).

seeds.title: Firm market note: card growth outlook (2026)
seeds.text: For planning we use growth of 13.8% a year in credit cards in use, taken from the CardScope India Cards Outlook 2026. No separate estimate was made. Sample data (simulated).

seeds.title: Firm case review: issuing bank and approval timelines
seeds.text: Across four recent card launches, setting up the issuing bank and getting approvals took 9 to 11 months. Method: review of project plans and regulator correspondence. Sample data (simulated).

seeds.title: Firm benchmark: end-to-end card launch set-up
seeds.text: In six launches we supported, the set-up phase before the first card was issued ranged from 8 to 14 months. Method: firm project database. Sample data (simulated).

seeds.title: CardScope India Cards Outlook 2026
seeds.text: We forecast that credit cards in use in India will grow 13.8% a year from 2025 to 2030. Method: issuer-level model calibrated on monthly bank returns. Sample data (simulated).

seeds.title: Card counts table (from central bank data)
seeds.text: Cards outstanding: 5.53 crore (Dec 2019); 10.80 crore (Dec 2024). Source: Reserve Bank of India. Sample data (simulated).

seeds.title: Card spending growth, 2025
seeds.text: Spending on credit cards grew 22% a year in 2025. This measures spend, not the number of cards. Method: bank-reported transaction values. Sample data (simulated).

seeds.title: Retail lending: acquisition cost by customer type
seeds.text: Banks report a 28 to 36% lower cost to sign up existing customers than new customers across retail products. Method: survey of 25 lenders. Sample data (simulated).

seeds.title: Retail lending: acquisition cost by customer type (2026 reprint)
seeds.text: Banks report a 28 to 36% lower cost to sign up existing customers than new customers across retail products. Method: survey of 25 lenders. Reprinted in 2026. Sample data (simulated).

seeds.title: Card holders by relationship with their main bank
seeds.text: 41% of retail customers who hold a credit card got it from their main bank. Method: household panel of 12,000 respondents. Sample data (simulated).

seeds.title: Card network certification times
seeds.text: The median time for a new issuer to complete card network certification is 4 months. Method: tracker of 18 programmes. Sample data (simulated).

seeds.title: Expert call: card industry adviser
seeds.text: New card issuers typically recover their sign-up costs in 20 to 30 months. It depends heavily on how many cards stay active. Sample data (simulated).

seeds.title: Expert call: former bank operations head
seeds.text: Onboarding an issuing bank and getting the approvals usually takes 10 to 12 months for a new issuer. Sample data (simulated).
